purpose: Front-door dispatch: decide deterministically whether a saved recipe still applies to an arriving workbook. Plan v1 sec.8.5 / sec.10 step 3. NO LLM is invoked anywhere in K.
framed_question: When an unknown workbook arrives, can a deterministic front door decide whether a saved recipe still applies -- without the filename, without silently running a stale recipe, and without escalating files it should have handled?
design_claim: The applicability predicate is not a new artifact: it is the step-2 recipe validator re-run against the candidate file. A recipe already declares everything its correctness depends on (bound sheets, header row, positional vs named columns, exclusions, and coverage totality), so re-validation answers 'does this still apply?' and the problem codes say what drifted.
replaces: Data-agents-demo _compute_structural_hash (DA-2): 5 preview rows + the filename. Too strict (next month's file never matches) and too shallow (blind to sheet identity and anything below row 5).
dispatch_algorithm: [1] LOOKUP  recipes whose data-role sheets ALL exist in the candidate (case-insensitive; the FORMAT is the key, never the filename). 0 -> DEFINE; >=2 -> AMBIGUOUS; 1 -> R
[2] APPLICABILITY  report = validate(R, candidate). If no field binding resolves at all -> DEFINE. Else if any binding or coverage problem -> REDEFINE_SCOPED with the delta named. Else -> [3]
[3] APPROVAL  content_sha256 == provenance.approved_recipe_sha256 AND approved_by set AND no blocking ambiguity -> EXECUTE (no model invoked); otherwise -> BLOCKED

edited_after_approval.note: body changed after approval; the stored approval hash is kept, so the content hash no longer matches

open_ambiguity.note: never approved; one blocking ambiguity still open

C2.why: THE DA-2 FIX: the filename is never consulted

C3.changed: two more products; the total row moves (A1:F11)
C3.why: PREREGISTERED OVER-ESCALATION (safe direction). More data rows is the ordinary monthly case, so EXECUTE is right. Recipe format v1 anchors data_region absolutely (Sales!5:8) and the total-row exclusion positionally (Sales!9), so rows 9-10 are claimed by nothing and the exclusion now points at a real product. A real gap in the FORMAT, surfaced by building the front door. Do NOT patch it during K.

C4.why: the NAMED binding @Tuote hits header_not_found, and col0 0 is then claimed by nothing

C5.changed: a Maa column inserted at B (A1:G9)
C5.why: THE D1 CASE. The positional binding B:D silently shifts to Maa/Tammi/Helmi and Maalis is left claimed by nothing. Coverage totality catches the silent shift that repo_reuse_map.md defect D1 describes -- a non-obvious positive claim under test here.

C6.why: nothing breaks, but 'which sheets matter?' is a definition decision and there is now a new one. Escalating is CORRECT here, not noise.

C7.why: lookup finds no recipe whose data sheet exists; nothing carries over

C8.changed: SAME dimensions (6 sheets, A1:F9, same headers); one product row is now a VÄLISUMMA subtotal
C8.why: PREREGISTERED FALSE EXECUTE (unsafe direction). Nothing about the shape changed, so re-validation is clean and the subtotal is consumed as a product, double-counting. A structural predicate CANNOT see this by construction. Included to measure the blind spot rather than discover it later. Do NOT add content heuristics during K.

C9.changed: nothing; the recipe store is empty

C10.changed: nothing; two recipes claim the same data sheet
C10.why: a human picks; the front door must not choose for them

C11.changed: nothing in the workbook; the RECIPE was edited after approval
C11.why: content hash != approved hash. 3E's gate-owns-authority applied to governance: a perfectly matching recipe must not run if the approval no longer covers it.

C12.changed: nothing in the workbook; the recipe has an open blocking ambiguity
C12.why: a recipe with an unanswered human question must not execute

grading.fidelity: dispatch(f) == predicted(f) -- a check on the AUTHOR's hand-simulation, not on the algorithm's correctness
grading.false_execute: { f : dispatch(f) == EXECUTE and ground_truth(f) != EXECUTE }
grading.over_escalation: { f : ground_truth(f) == EXECUTE and dispatch(f) != EXECUTE }

decision_table.condition: fidelity on all 12 AND false_execute == ['C8'] AND over_escalation == ['C3']
decision_table.outcome: PASS_AS_PREDICTED -- the front door behaves exactly as designed, with two named costs
FAIL_UNSAFE -- a stale recipe would run on a changed file. Record; do not tune
FAIL_NOISE -- the macro does not pay off. Record; do not tune
FAIL_BASELINE -- the repeat case does not work, which is the whole point

decision_table.condition: fidelity fails but the code matches the frozen spec
decision_table.outcome: RESULT, not a bug: the author mis-predicted their own algorithm. Record; do not amend spec or prediction

hard_stop: Dispatch only. No execution of any recipe (step 6).
No changes to the frozen referent grammar (referent-grammar-v1).
No changes to recipe format v1 -- including NOT adding data_region: 'remainder', however tempting C3 makes it. Fixing the format mid-experiment destroys the measurement.
stated_limitations: Lookup keys on 'the recipe's data sheets all exist', which is weak: many recipes could match on a common sheet name. C10 exercises the AMBIGUOUS branch but the lookup key itself is not the object under test here.
12 in-lab candidates derived from one workbook. A controlled replay, not a prevalence estimate of how providers actually change files (the UQ-1 question, kept separate).
The predicate is STRUCTURAL by construction. C8 measures exactly what that cannot see; catching content-semantics drift needs row-level evidence and is out of scope.
Deterministic and fully repeatable: no LLM, no seeds, no sampling. The n=1 reliability caveat attached to every LLM probe in this programme does not apply.
